text.p: The United States energy regulator concluded that the proposed Portland Natural Gas Transmission System was "environmentally acceptable" in a Draft Environmental Impact Statement issued on Friday, the project's backers said.

Friday's U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission statement, which deemed the $302 million project acceptable with staff-recommended mitigation measures, meant it was on track to meet its November 1998 in-service date, PNGTS said.
Final FERC approval of the pipeline, which would ship 178 million cubic feet of gas per day into New England, was expected at the end of August, it said.

PNGTS said the statement assessed potential environmental impacts of about 186 miles of mainline and laterals to be installed between Pittsburg, New Hampshire and Westbrook, Maine, plus 39 miles of mainline and laterals to be built jointly by PNGTS and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline.
Partners in the project include Bay State Gas Co, Gaz Metropolitain & Co LP, MCN Energy Group Inc , TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and US Generating Co.
